title: Louhi: The Sun and Moon Hidden
subtitle: A night without the familiar lights

hiding.author: Elias Lönnrot, compiler and editor
hiding.locator: Rune XLVII · Louhi steals Sun, Moon, and Fire; Rune XLVII · Louhi steals Sun, Moon, and Fire, normalized characters 519-1206
hiding.excerpt: Louhi, hostess of Pohyola, Northland’s old and toothless wizard, Makes the Sun and Moon her captives; In her arms she takes fair Luna From her cradle in the birch-tree, Calls the Sun down from his station, From the fir-tree’s bending branches, Carries them to upper Northland, To the darksome Sariola; Hides the Moon, no more to glimmer, In a rock of many colors; Hides the Sun, to shine no longer, In the iron-banded mountain; Thereupon these words she utters: “Moon of gold and Sun of silver, Hide your faces in the caverns Of Pohyola’s dismal mountain; Shine no more to gladden Northland, Till I come to give ye freedom, Drawn by coursers nine in number, Sable coursers of one mother!
hiding.note: Verbatim English verse translated by John Martin Crawford from Lönnrot's nineteenth-century compilation of oral poetry; not a transcript of one ancient or single oral witness.

narrativeBlocks.title: The mistress of the North
narrativeBlocks.body: Louhi is the fierce mistress of Pohjola — the cold, dark land of the north — witch-queen, bargain-maker, and the epic's great antagonist.

narrativeBlocks.title: The theft of sun and moon
narrativeBlocks.body: She takes the sun and moon from the sky and hides them in her mountain — the world below goes dark and cold, the days measured only by darkness.

narrativeBlocks.title: Ukko's own fire stolen
narrativeBlocks.body: Even the fire in heaven is caught — the world's light itself is her captive, and the heroes must go fetch it.

narrativeBlocks.title: The counterstroke
narrativeBlocks.body: Vainamoinen and Ilmarinen go to Pohjola for the sun and moon — and the quest that follows is the Kalevala's great expedition against the dark.

narrativeBlocks.title: The North as character
narrativeBlocks.body: Pohjola is not just a place — it is the cold, dark opposite of everything the singers' south values: the myth makes geography into villain.
